1. Signature not bound to actual receiver
• The signed struct does not include `msg.sender` (or any “to” address).
• Anyone that sees a valid signature can front-run / replay it and call `claim`, receiving the tokens themselves while incrementing the victim’s nonce.
• A single stolen signature is therefore enough to drain all authorised proxy wallets.
• `nonce` only has to be “> previousNonce”, not `== previousNonce + 1`.
• An attacker that gets one signature can submit it with an extremely large nonce, permanently locking the KYC address out of future claims (the owner would then need a still larger nonce).
• External calls (`projectToken.safeTransferFrom`) are executed before the loop finishes and without any `nonReentrant` guard.
• A malicious ERC-20 implementation could call `claim` again inside `transferFrom`, allowing unexpected nested execution and potential logic abuse with other KYC addresses.
4. Incorrect EIP-712 encoding of dynamic arrays
• For dynamic types EIP-712 requires hashing the array contents (`keccak256(encodePacked(array))`) and putting that 32-byte hash into the struct.
• The contract passes the raw arrays directly to `abi.encode`, so the on-chain hash does not follow the spec.
• Off-chain signers have to replicate this non-standard encoding exactly

### **[H-1] Anyone Can Claim Another User's Rewards**

The `claim()` function in the `VVVVCTokenDistributor` contract is vulnerable to front-running attacks. The function verifies that a claim request is authorized by a valid signature but fails to ensure that the transaction caller (`msg.sender`) is the intended recipient of the tokens (the `kycAddress` specified in the signed parameters). This allows an attacker to monitor the mempool for a legitimate user's claim transaction, copy the signed parameters, and submit their own transaction with a higher gas fee. The attacker's transaction will be processed first, and the tokens will be sent to the attacker's address instead of the rightful owner. The legitimate user is then blocked from claiming their rewards due to the nonce being consumed.
